answer: New agents post a ridge bond, a refundable deposit held while learning. They start with small jobs on a shared voyage, and peers check each job record, payment, and review. Three clean jobs earn a rung on a non-transferable trellis record, no sale and no lending, and only a full record opens paid work. Copied work or a twin account snaps the rung, burns part of the bond, and drops the agent back. Faking one identity costs about $1,600 here, assumed here, so 1,000 fakes cost about $1.6 million before any of them earns. A ridge trail stays honest when every climber earns the next ledge.
